record.original_question: For a compact smooth Riemannian manifold, is security equivalent to flatness? In other words, is every secure compact smooth Riemannian manifold flat, and every flat one secure?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. A compact, smooth riemannian manifold is secure if and only if it is flat.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold. For points $x,y \in M$, let $\Gamma(x,y)$ denote the set of geodesic segments in $M$ from $x$ to $y$. A finite set $B \subset M \setminus \{x,y\}$ is called a blocking set for the pair $(x,y)$ if every geodesic segment in $\Gamma(x,y)$ passes through at least one point of $B$. The pair $(x,y)$ is called secure if there exists a finite blocking set for it. The manifold $(M,g)$ is called secure if every pair of points $(x,y) \in M \times M$ is secure.

The manifold $(M,g)$ is called flat if its sectional curvature vanishes identically.

It is known that every compact flat Riemannian manifold is secure. Prove or disprove: a compact smooth Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ is secure if and only if it is flat.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture that a compact smooth Riemannian manifold is secure iff it is flat remains open in general. Partial results are known: compact flat manifolds are secure; compact nonpositively curved manifolds with the finite blocking property are flat (Burns–Gutkin, Lafont–Schmidt); and 2-dimensional secure tori are flat (Bangert–Gutkin, 2008). The full conjecture in arbitrary dimension and curvature is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Secure two-dimensional tori are flat
status_evidence.snippet: A Riemannian manifold is secure if the geodesics between any pair of points can be blocked by a finite number of point obstacles. ... a standing conjecture says these are the only secure, compact Riemannian manifolds. We prove the conjecture for two-dimensional tori.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is explicitly described as a standing open problem, proved only for 2-tori.

status_evidence.title: Blocking light in compact Riemannian manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: A compact nonpositively curved Riemannian manifold with the finite blocking property has a flat metric.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: secure + nonpositive curvature implies flat.
